To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the occurrence of NSPs in a population sample was predominantly predicted by environmental sensitivity, perceived proximity to BS, perceived control and avoidance behavior.

(1) perceived proximity to base station and powerline, and (2) perceived environmental sensitivity, are the most important determinants of NSP, and (3) there is no evidence that the actual proximity to BS and powerlines contributes to the report of symptoms.

(i) the occurrence of NSPs is not related to actual distance to EMF sources (BS and powerlines); (ii) the report of NSPS is associated with perceived proximity to BS; (iii) the report of perceived proximity to BS is associated with self-reported environmental sensitivity, perceived control and avoidance behavior; (iv) self-reported environmental sensitivity moderates the relation between perceived BS and NSPS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a psychological component of the occurrence of EMFS-related NSPS.
the role of psychological components in the association between EMF and NSPS, and not with the role of EMF exposure.
the role of psychological factors in the relation between EMF and symptoms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current results are consistent with a psychogenic hypothesis, but do not rule out a possible causal role of EMF.
the association between NSPS and EMF exposure is not likely to be due to EMF, but rather to psychological components and perceived exposure.
the occurrence of NSPs is not caused by EMFs emitted by base stations or power lines, but rather that psychological factors are important determinants of symptom occurrence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the occurrence of EMFS-related NSPS can best be explained by psychological characteristics.
perceived proximity to BS, environmental sensitivity, perceived control and coping behavior are associated with the occurrence of NSPs.
the current study supports the hypothesis that the association between EMF and NSPS may be partly due to psychological components.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the association between perceived proximity to base station and NSPS is moderated by perceived environmental sensitivity.
the perception of EMF sources may be more important than actual exposure.
perceived proximity to BS is a determinant for NSPS.
